description: Base Renovate configuration for sbaerlocher repositories

packageRules.description: Pre-1.0 packages: SemVer does not guarantee backward compatibility; treat any non-patch bump as potentially breaking and require manual review.

sbaerlocher/.github - date tags, no digest pinning, weekly rollout. merge.yml cuts a YYYY-MM-DD tag on every push to main, so a daily schedule opens one PR per workflow change in every consumer repo (26 tags in the 30 days to 2026-09-02). Batching the rollout to Monday keeps the rolling-release model while cutting consumer PR churn to roughly 4 per month. `groupSlug` is what carries the schedule, not `groupName`: Renovate derives the branch from `slugify(groupSlug ?? groupName)` and evaluates `schedule` per branch, and packageRules merge last-wins per key - so the `groupSlug: all-non-major` from the non-major rule above survives a bare `groupName` override here (a tag bump like 2026-08-31 -> 2026-09-04 is a minor under this rule's own regex versioning, so that rule does match). Without an explicit groupSlug the bump lands on `renovate/all-non-major` and this window either does nothing or defers every other non-major update with it. `minimumReleaseAge` is deliberately waived: the Monday window is itself the soak, and a 1-day gate would push any tag cut over the weekend past the window and on to the next Monday, an 8-day lag. An urgent workflow fix is still reachable on demand via the Dependency Dashboard checkbox.

Docker registries that never report a release timestamp. Renovate's docker datasource reads timestamps only from Docker Hub (`tag_last_pushed`), so images on these hosts have no age to check and the global `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-optional` would log a 'did not have a releaseTimestamp' warning on every run. Waiving the age gate here records that deliberately per registry; a warning that still appears points at a dependency not listed here and needs a look, not a blanket waiver. This also lifts the 7-day gate on majors and on critical platform charts for these registries; that gate could never work here, because without a timestamp there is no age to wait for. Keep the registry list identical in all four waiver rules (two here, two in renovate-kubernetes.json) and in AGENTS.md.

Same registries when the host sits in registryUrls instead of the package name (OCI Helm charts, Fleet OCI custom manager). Regex instead of a glob so the bare host form `https://ghcr.io` from `registryUrlTemplate` matches as well. renovate-kubernetes.json repeats both rules after its helmv3 OCI rule, which would otherwise put the 5-day gate back. This also lifts the 7-day gate on majors and on critical platform charts for these registries; that gate could never work here, because without a timestamp there is no age to wait for. Keep the registry list identical in all four waiver rules (two here, two in renovate-kubernetes.json) and in AGENTS.md.

git-refs never reports a release timestamp: Renovate's git-refs datasource exposes ref names and commit SHAs only (no releaseTimestamp anywhere in lib/modules/datasource/git-refs). Digest updates of SHA-pinned git dependencies, such as the caddy-tailscale plugin in infrastructure, therefore have no age to check and raised the 'did not have a releaseTimestamp' warning on every run. Waived explicitly like the docker registries above, and only for digest updates (the case seen in the Mend log, datasource git-refs): if git-refs ever starts reporting commit dates, branch or tag updates keep their cooldown. Other timestamp-less sources (for example git-tags) are waived only once a log shows them, not ahead of time.

Digest updates of grafana/grafana have no release timestamp in the Mend runs of tsmetrics, savvy and velometrics (2026-11-05), while other Docker Hub images in the same runs (prom/prometheus, golang, alpine) keep theirs. The cause is not established: grafana/grafana has 2045 tags and Docker Hub answers page 11 of the tag list with 403, but golang (5113 tags, same 403) keeps its timestamps, so tag count alone does not explain it. Limited to digest updates, the only case the logs show, so minor/patch/major updates keep their cooldown if timestamps come back. Remove once Renovate reports timestamps for this image again; add other images only after a log names them.

Custom regex managers tracking Docker images via env-var markers (e.g. `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=foo` over `IMAGE_VERSION: '1.2.3'`) cannot accept a digest — the regex captures only the version. Disable digest pinning to avoid 'Digest is not updated' branch failures.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Monthly, the whole first Wednesday (day of month AND day of week must both match in Renovate cron), away from the Monday batch that bumps the preset tag and GitHub Actions. Trade-off: vulnerabilityAlerts only cover dependencies declared in a package file, so a vulnerable transitive dependency can now wait up to about five weeks for this refresh instead of one. minimumReleaseAge is null because a lock file refresh has no release timestamp: with the global 3-day age it raised 'upgrade(s) did not have a releaseTimestamp' on the lock-file-maintenance branch every run (console.sbaerlo.ch Mend log, 2026-11-05 19:22).
